generation.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Electric Power Monthly (Form EIA-923), net generation by state and source, grouped by the ERW (docs/methods/generation_mix.md)
generation.hourly_reason: No public source gives a state's generation by the hour; the hourly picture is by balancing authority, in the Grid tool.

retail.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Form EIA-861M, retail sales and average price by state and sector
retail.revenue_note: Revenue is EIA's sales times EIA's average price for the same month and sector. EIA computes its average price as revenue over sales, so the product gives EIA's revenue to within the price's rounding (one tenth of a dollar a MWh).

plants.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Preliminary Monthly Electric Generator Inventory (Form EIA-860M)
plants.unit: MW (nameplate and net summer); MWh (storage energy)
plants.retired_note: EIA-860M's retired sheet as the ERW's table holds it: the generators retired in its window, not every retirement since 2001.

co2.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, State Electricity Profiles, emissions by state by fuel
co2.unit: metric tons of CO2; kg of CO2 per MWh

gas.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Natural Gas Monthly, consumption by end use and production by state

energy.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, State Energy Data System

by_sector_reason.commercial: the warehouse's SEDS tables hold the commercial sector's electricity and natural gas, not its total energy
by_sector_reason.transportation: the warehouse's SEDS tables hold the transportation sector's electricity and natural gas, not its total energy

disposition.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, State Electricity Profiles, source and disposition
disposition.note: Net interstate trade is EIA's figure, a line of the disposition: positive where the state sent more electricity to other states than it took in from them, below zero where it took in more.

serving.source: U.S. Census Bureau county population estimates, and Form EIA-861's utilities and balancing authorities by county, as the ERW's table eia_county_region joins them

by_authority.reason: its utilities name no balancing authority in EIA-861's sales file

serving.basis: Each county counts once, whole, for its primary authority: the one whose utilities serve most of the county's customers in EIA-861. A county two authorities share is counted for its primary one.

large_load_laws.source: The ERW's large-load research files, each law read at its legislature's or regulator's own page

laws.title: To repeal sections ... RSMo, and to enact in lieu thereof thirty-two new sections relating to utilities
laws.threshold: customers reasonably projected to have an annual peak demand of 100 MW or more, for electrical corporations serving more than 250,000 customers; 50 MW or more for those serving 250,000 or fewer customers as of 1 January 2025
laws.requirements: cost allocation: each electrical corporation must develop and submit to the Commission tariff schedules for these customers that should reasonably ensure their rates reflect their representative share of the costs to serve them and prevent other classes' rates from reflecting unjust or unreasonable costs of serving them; the Commission may order similar tariffs for customers below the thresholds [https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=393.130 (read 2026-11-14) p. 1, 393.130.7: "shall develop and submit to the commission schedules to include in the electrical corporation's service tariff" | https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=393.130 (read 2026-11-14) p. 1, 393.130.7: "The schedules should reasonably ensure such customers' rates will reflect the customers' representative share of the costs incurred to serve the customers and prevent other customer classes' rates from reflecting any unjust or unreasonable costs arising from service to such customers." | https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=393.130 (read 2026-11-14) p. 1, 393.130.7: "The commission may order electrical corporations to submit similar tariffs to reasonably ensure that the rates of customers who are reasonably projected to have annual peak demands below the above-referenced levels"]

laws.title: To repeal section 393.130, RSMo, and to enact in lieu thereof two new sections relating to the regulation of large load electric customers.
laws.threshold: would lower the 393.130.7 threshold for the larger electrical corporations from 100 MW to 50 MW of annual peak demand; the emergency curtailment duty applies above 25 MW of peak demand
laws.requirements: curtailment or backup generation: a large load facility with peak demand above 25 MW would have to implement an emergency curtailment system letting the serving utility temporarily reduce or suspend its service in firm load emergencies; it may switch to self-supported backup generation [p. 9, 393.325.8(1): "Any large load facility with a peak electrical ... demand of greater than twenty-five megawatts shall implement ... an emergency curtailment system for temporary reduction or" | p. 9, 393.325.8(2): "switch to backup generation that is self-supported during"] || other: an annual payment by each large load facility toward low-income energy assistance: 250,000 dollars up to 25 MW, 500,000 dollars from 25 to 50 MW, 1,000,000 dollars above 50 MW [p. 9, 393.325.7(c): "fifty megawatts of electricity shall pay one million dollars."]

severance.reason: the severance tool holds Texas, Louisiana, New Mexico only
